# Lighting and Wiring Modifications

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Route wires and install seal-tight connectors with silicone to secure lighting modifications. [t4]

Cut wires in the middle of the stalk circuit board to allow easy reversion. [t56]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Cut the wires in the middle of the stalk circuit board instead of removing them entirely to allow easy reversion to stock.
2. Loop the cut wires through a provided hole rather than breaking off the white tab on the connector.
3. Run one wire from the light switch stalk to the IDPM fuse box located in the engine bay, routing it through the firewall.
4. Ground the second wire (approx. 1-2 feet long) to the metal frame underneath the dash inside the cabin.
5. Prepare a relay by cutting wires #30 and #85 to be approximately 5-6 inches long each.
6. Connect the wire from the light switch stalk into terminal #86 on the relay, which previously lacked a connection.
7. Attach an add-a-circuit fuse tap to terminal #85 on the relay using a spade connector modified by filing it down for size.
8. Secure another spade connector (also filed smaller) onto terminal #30 of the relay.
9. Plug the spade connector into the F10 slot in the IDPM and insert the add-a-circuit fuse tap into the F7 slot.
10. Route both wires from the light switch stalk and the 12V power wire through a hole provided in the fuse box lid or frame.
11. [Partial] Connect the red 12V wire to the battery terminal.

_Procedure reported by [t56]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-fog-lights-by-pass-without-giving-up-factory-switch.561/>_

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Remove the nut from the connector before pulling the harness inside [t4]
- Use a rubber washer if available, or apply extra silicone on its own [t4]
- Ensure no air remains trapped to prevent rust at the drilled spot [t4]
- [Partial] Use mechanical protection only on the part inside the dash [t4]
- [Partial] Tape wires together for easier installation of pillar covers [t4]
- Choose slim enough lights for a Dephep rack in closed position [t4]
- Use heat-shrink tubing with a thin wall of glue over solder joints [t4]
- Use thin-wall glue heat-shrink tubing so it reduces in size and melts [t4]
- Orient the box with an opening in the bottom so water drips out [t4]
- Ensure all wire strands are fully crimped by bending the wire if needed [t4]
- Essential for non-100% sealed slim lights like the Hella 500 [t4]
- [Partial] Use any type of relay. [t56]
- Ensure the wire from the stalk is about 1-2 feet long for grounding. [t56]
